item.title: Italy slaps Apple with $115 million fine over App Store privacy rules
item.description: Regulators argue that rules harms Apple’s business partners and goes beyond what’s necessary to protect user privacy.

item.title: Texas judge blocks app store age verification law
item.description: CCIA says the law would create a sweeping censorship system and force teens and parents to hand over personal data just to exist online.

item.title: AI gets the blame for 55,000 layoffs, but CFOs are the real culprits
item.description: Entry-level roles are quietly disappearing as companies convince themselves that a chatbot can do a junior employee’s job, even when it absolutely cannot.

item.title: WhatsApp channels are getting pop quizzes
item.description: Quizzes live alongside polls, but they come with one important twist: admins have to pick the correct answer before hitting publish.

item.title: James Bond will return in the new game, just not in March
item.description: The extra time is going toward polish and refinement.

item.title: Gmail finally lets you fix that cringey old email address
item.description: The old address doesn’t disappear into the void, it becomes an alternate email tied to your account.

item.title: Amazon turns Alexa into an actual personal assistant
item.description: Alexa+ is supposed to do the searching and hiring professionals, comparing and booking flights and hotels, and also paying, for you.

item.title: OpenAI’s new job pays $555K to stop AI from ruining everything
item.description: It’s a stressful job. Try not to mess up. No pressure.

item.title: Ubisoft pulls Rainbow Six Siege offline as attackers cause chaos
item.description: The ban notification pop-ups were hijacked to slowly scroll out the lyrics to It Wasn’t Me

item.title: Samsung’s year-end sale resurrects Black Friday deals from the dead
item.description: Samsung's year-end sale is unleashing unbeatable deals on monitors, TVs, and appliances, with extra savings for students, military, and select business employees.
